rationale: No supported optimization is clearly applicable without weakening coverage or violating a stated contraindication. The workflow already enables Bundler dependency caching via `bundler-cache: true` for every matrix cell except jruby-head on windows (where it is intentionally disabled because the frozen install fails), so adding a separate `actions/cache` step for `vendor/bundle` is contraindicated by P-LIT-GHA-CACHE / P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE: "An equivalent cache already exists." The measured experiment (batch-hiruni...) used a different matrix (gemfile + DB services) and its outcome is unmeasured/null, so it does not override the contraindication here. Changing `fail-fast` to true (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) is contraindicated because the workflow explicitly sets `fail-fast: false` with the comment "run all tests so we see which gem/ruby combinations break" — every matrix outcome and full failure diagnostics are required. Other patterns lack prerequisites (no Bazel, no Python/pip, no scheduled workflows, no representative duration history for a custom timeout) or carry required-check/cancellation safety concerns (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) while required_checks are unverified. Build and test coverage is therefore preserved as-is.
